output:
**What I found**

The line-limit gate no longer blocks anything. Each time it goes red, a script rebuilds the exception list from the current tree and the result is committed along with whatever change caused the failure. That is why it has stayed green: over 12 days the list was rewritten 34 times and grew from 41 to 58 modules, and none of the 17 additions was named in a commit message. The fix is to make the list shrink on its own but grow only when a change names the specific module and says why (the record calls this RATCHET).

There is a second problem. The list only records whether a module is exempt, so an exempt module can keep growing with no limit at all.

**Why it matters**

Every red run currently turns into an approval. The 17 new oversized modules entered without anyone deciding to accept them, and the 41 older ones can keep growing without the gate noticing. If nothing changes, the list keeps growing on most commits and the line limit only applies to modules that have never broken it.

**Do this first**

1. Replace the regeneration script with a reconcile step. Use the algorithm in `.claude/skills/gate-lifecycle/references/ratchet.md`:
   - New or grown entries fail the gate unless the change names them, for example `--accept-growth <path>`. There is no flag that accepts everything.
   - A red run writes nothing to the baseline.
   - Stale entries are removed.
   - Each entry stores the module's current line count instead of just its presence, so exempt modules can't grow either.
   - Unit tests cover all four outcomes (refused, accepted, shrunk, stale). The refused case runs in CI and is the gate's proof that it can still go red.

Follow-ups:
- Go through the 17 unnamed additions. For each one, either accept it in a commit that names the module and the reason, or split the module and drop the entry.
- Give the baseline file an owner, for example a CODEOWNERS entry, so any growth gets reviewed.

**What I did not check**

- Which 17 modules were added, and in which commits: `git log -p --follow -- <baseline.json>`, and `git diff <commit from 12 days ago> HEAD -- <baseline.json>`.
- Whether CI runs the regeneration script or people run it by hand: `git grep -n <script name> -- .github ci scripts`.
- Whether some exempt modules already shrank below the limit, which would make their entries stale: run the line counter against the baseline.
- No repository files were read. This record rests on what you described.

```text
Gate:         source-module line-limit check + JSON exception baseline, merge gate (CI)
Stage:        merge gate (as described; not re-placed)
Trigger:      churn — baseline rewritten 34× in 12 days, grew 41→58 with no named decision
Proof:        UNPROVEN — red runs occurred but were overwritten by regeneration; no negative control asserts that unnamed growth stays red
Scope:        declared: all source modules ≤ limit except a fixed debt list
              effective: every module present at the last red run, listed entries unbounded in size
              delta: any new oversized module, and any growth inside a listed module, is no longer checked
Baseline:     58 entries, growing; last accepted growth: none named (17 additions, 0 named)
Status:       BLOCKING (nominally); effectively self-approving
Decision:     RATCHET
Guard:        unnamed growth refused by reconcile; red run writes nothing; per-entry line counts; baseline has a named owner
Handoff:      none (blocking semantics stay with ci-cd-reliability-architecture if the gate's exit behavior changes)
Next action:  replace the regenerate-and-commit script with reconcile (per-entry --accept-growth, stale removal, size values) plus a CI unit test of the refused case
Verification: Not run — no repository was inspected; close with the reconcile refused-case test going red in CI
```
